howto.name: Add a recording
howto.text: Select an audio file up to 500 MB, such as a voice memo, a meeting recording or an interview.

howto.name: Choose where it runs
howto.text: On this device uses Whisper in your browser: Tiny, about 41 MB, is faster, and Base, about 74 MB, is more accurate. The model downloads once and is cached. With your own API key, the audio goes to your chosen provider instead.

howto.name: Transcribe
howto.text: Start the transcription. On-device speed depends on your computer, so a long recording can take a while.

howto.name: Export the text
howto.text: Copy the transcript, download it as a .txt file, or download timed subtitles as .srt.

faq.a: Not with the on-device engine: the audio is decoded and transcribed in your browser. What is downloaded is the Whisper model itself, fetched once from a public model host and cached. If you choose your own API key, the audio goes from your browser directly to that provider, not through PrivaTools.

faq.q: Tiny or Base — which model should I use?
faq.a: Base is noticeably more accurate, particularly with accents, background noise and unusual words, at roughly twice the download and a slower run. Start with Base unless your device is slow or the recording is very clear.
Yes. Download the .srt file, which carries the timings with each line and loads into video editors and players. Review it, since automatic timings and punctuation are rarely perfect.
Whisper is multilingual and detects the language itself. Accuracy is best for widely spoken languages and drops for less common ones, especially with the smaller Tiny model.

The on-device engine runs on your own processor, so speed depends on your hardware and the recording length. A long meeting on a modest laptop takes time; your own API key moves the work to the provider.
Good on clear speech, weaker on crosstalk, heavy accents, poor microphones and specialist vocabulary. Treat the transcript as a draft and check names and numbers before relying on it.
